question.text: Per SEBI framework on AIF distribution/placement commissions, what is the rule for Category III AIFs charging distribution fee?

answer.text: Category III AIFs can charge upfront distribution fee up to 2% of commitment

Category III AIFs can charge distribution fee on equal trail basis only; no upfront distribution fee can be charged directly or indirectly, and any distribution fee paid shall be only from the management fee received by the manager
Category III AIFs can charge distribution fee up to one-third upfront and the rest on trail
Category III AIFs are exempt from distribution fee regulations

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 13.7.3, Category III AIFs shall charge distribution/placement fee, if any, to investors only on equal trail basis — no upfront distribution fee shall be charged directly or indirectly. Further, any distribution fee paid shall be only from the management fee received by the managers of such Category III AIFs. Category I/II AIFs may pay up to one-third upfront and balance on equal trail. The Trap: Option C is the Cat I/II rule, not Cat III. This differential treatment is a common trap. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B (Cat III distributor) exam tests this as distributor-commission ceiling. XIX-C requires manager to know the upfront ban and the 'only from management fee' constraint. Manager's Pro-Tip: When modelling Cat III fund economics, budget the entire distribution fee as a deduction from management fee. Trying to charge distribution fee separately to the fund = regulatory breach.
